description: After fz-bin.9 filters the dead reducer publication boundary, fixtures2/behavior/range_enumerable.fz reaches Enumerable.Range.slice/1. Native run prints the reduce/count/member outputs, then panics in runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs: fz_closure_get_capture_ref idx=0 expected closure ref, got tag ValueKind(0) word=0xa. Backend interp prints the two reduce outputs, then fails with 'backend value 5 is unbound'. Research indicates the returned slicer callable tuple field/capture path is passing a captured range integer where the closure self/boxed callable should be. This blocks re-enabling range_enumerable run/interp/build after the fz-bin.9 boundary publication fix.

comments.text: Created from fz-bin.9 verification. Current native run reaches Range slice after printing reduce/count/member outputs, then aborts at fz_closure_get_capture_ref with tagged int 0xa as closure self. Current backend interp reaches the second reduce output, then reports backend value 5 is unbound. The boundary-publication ambiguity from fz-bin.9 is no longer observed.

Blocked by fz-bin.17. Current native crash is not the direct closure-call fast path alone: dumps show Enumerable.slice returns {:ok, n, slicer} with the callable field flattened through the return/resume payload. main__e0__resume_24 receives four params and captures v2 as slicer; v2 is the integer capture 10. main__e0__resume_25 then calls fz_closure_get_capture_ref through that value and aborts. Experimental native-only fixes either failed to affect the CLIF or broke direct-only callables with no boundary, so the prerequisite is to publish/materialize a first-class boundary for tuple-returned callable fields that later resume as closures.

title: Returned Range slicer callable is called with captured integer as closure self
